subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Urothelial carcinoma: staging, systemic immunotherapy and targeted antibody-drug conjugates

steps.tx: Management of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer focuses on complete diagnostic eradication and preventing recurrence. High-quality **Transurethral resection** of bladder tumour with detrusor muscle in the specimen is the critical initial staging step. For high-risk non-muscle invasive lesions, intravesical **Bacillus Calmette-Guerin** immunotherapy following resection triggers an intense local mucosal immune reaction, reducing recurrences and preventing progression to muscle invasion.

steps.tx: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer requires aggressive multimodal therapy with curative intent. **Neoadjuvant cisplatin-based** combination chemotherapy with either **gemcitabine** plus **cisplatin** or dose-dense MVAC improves overall survival by approximately 5% to 8% compared with surgery alone. Following neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy provides definitive local oncological control.

steps.tx: First-line systemic therapy for advanced urothelial carcinoma has been redefined by the phase 3 **EV-302** trial. Combining the Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate **enfortumab vedotin** with the PD-1 inhibitor **pembrolizumab** doubled median progression-free and overall survival compared with standard platinum-based chemotherapy. This combination represents the new frontline standard of care irrespective of cisplatin eligibility or PD-L1 expression levels.

steps.tx: For patients treated with frontline platinum-based cytotoxic chemotherapy, switch maintenance immunotherapy provides significant survival benefits. In the **JAVELIN Bladder 100** trial, administering maintenance **avelumab** to patients whose disease had not progressed following 4 to 6 cycles of **gemcitabine** plus platinum prolonged overall survival significantly. Initiating avelumab maintenance immediately consolidates response and delays disease recurrence.

steps.tx: Activating genomic alterations in fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 occur in approximately 15% to 20% of metastatic urothelial tumours. **Erdafitinib** is an oral pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved for susceptible FGFR3 or FGFR2 genetic alterations. In the phase 3 **THOR trial**, erdafitinib significantly prolonged overall survival compared to single-agent chemotherapy in patients who had previously progressed on immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

steps.tx: Adjuvant systemic immunotherapy provides an effective therapeutic option for patients with resected high-risk disease. In the **CheckMate 274** trial, **Adjuvant nivolumab** administered for 1 year significantly prolonged disease-free survival compared to placebo in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer following radical cystectomy. Benefit was particularly striking in patients displaying tumour cell PD-L1 expression of 1% or higher.

steps.tx: **Upper tract urothelial carcinoma** involves the renal pelvis and ureter and exhibits a high association with hereditary Lynch syndrome. Standard surgical management consists of radical **nephroureterectomy** with an en-bloc excision of a bladder cuff. A single postoperative dose of intravesical chemotherapy within 2 to 10 days significantly reduces the incidence of secondary bladder tumour recurrences.

steps.tx: For patients wishing to avoid cystectomy, **Trimodality bladder preservation** provides an established curative alternative. The approach combines maximal transurethral tumour resection with concurrent **chemoradiotherapy** utilizing radiosensitising cisplatin or 5-fluorouracil plus mitomycin C. Long-term oncological outcomes and cancer-specific survival rates compare favourably with primary radical cystectomy in carefully selected candidates with unifocal disease.
